10.1002_advs.78531: Gel‐based wet electrodes remain the gold standard for electrophysiology, but gel dehydration limits recordings. Existing dry electrodes partially address this limitation but suffer from high interfacial impedance. Here, a carbon fiber‐based porous electrode (CFPE) is reported, comprising a three‐dimensional conductive network coated with poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS). The CFPE establishes contact at hairy‐scalp sites with an impedance of approximately 10 kΩ·cm 2 . On the forearm, its impedance at 10 Hz without skin preparation is 11.09 ± 1.03 kΩ·cm 2 , compared with 13.57 ± 2.07 kΩ·cm 2 for wet electrodes. After 6 h of wear, CFPE impedance reaches 1.3 times its initial value without skin preparation or gel, whereas wet‐electrode impedance reaches 56 times its initial value when applied with skin preparation and conductive gel. High‐fidelity electrocardiography, electromyography, and electroencephalography signals are captured with correlation coefficients exceeding 90% and signal‐to‐noise ratios comparable to wet electrodes. The CFPE further resolves microvolt‐level speech‐evoked frequency‐following responses (FFR) and long‐latency responses (LLR), with fidelity comparable to wet electrodes and significantly higher LLR SNR. These results demonstrate gel‐free acquisition of weak neural biomarkers, opening a pathway toward prolonged, preparation‐free neurophysiology.
10.1016_j.ces.2026.123431: • Coupling between the shrinking core and the Eulerian-Eulerian multiphase model is derived. • It is applied to redox chemical kinetic model of ilmenite for CLC. • Validation is done using lab-scale fluidized bed batch reactor and 300 W CLC reactor. • OpenFOAM program codes and configuration files of simulations are openly shared. One of the main barriers to the implementation of chemical looping combustion (CLC) on an industrial scale is the lack of knowledge about its operation at such scales. As a first step towards modeling industrial CLC devices, a consistent coupling between the shrinking core model (SCM) and the Eulerian-Eulerian multiphase framework with multicomponent phases was derived. This coupling enforces the constant volume assumption of a solid particle and allows for simple and consistent control of the oxygen transfer capacity. The derived approach was then applied to the chemical kinetic model of ilmenite redox reactions, which was sourced from the literature and was based on thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) data. Important corrections were made to the kinetic model parameters to ensure consistency with the present methodology, and the result was verified using a zero-dimensional TGA simulation setup. The methodology was further validated using experimental data from the literature for a laboratory-scale batch fluidized bed reactor. Three-dimensional simulations and an analytical one-dimensional quasi-steady-state model, derived on the basis of the coupling, have shown very close results to each other. However, as also previously observed in the literature, the conversion rates of H 2 were severely underestimated by the TGA-based kinetic model. Finally, the developed approach was applied to a 300 W CLC reactor, previously experimentally studied at Chalmers University. The agreement with the experimental data was reasonably good, but the reactivity of H 2 was higher than that reported in the experiments. The chemistry model source code and simulation configurations are made openly available.
